content.text:
Mostly because your Claude wrapper forces Fable 5.1 to start at **`max` effort** ([home.nix](/home/thom/src/github.com/tteggel/.dotfiles/home/home.nix:16)).

That compounds several Fable behaviors:

- Adaptive thinking is always enabled.
- At `max`, Fable can reason for much longer and may effectively draft a deliverable in thinking before producing it again as visible output.
- Those hidden thinking tokens count as output tokens, and prior thinking blocks remain in later context as input tokens.
- Coding loops may make sequential rather than batched tool calls, creating extra turns and context re-reads.

Anthropic explicitly describes effort as Fable’s main intelligence-versus-cost control and recommends starting at `high`; `medium` reportedly approaches Fable 5 quality at lower cost. [Fable 5.1 prompting guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-1)

There’s also a display effect in your setup: Fable has a native **1M-token context**, but you force auto-compaction at **256k** ([settings.json](/home/thom/src/github.com/tteggel/.dotfiles/config/claude/settings.json:3)). Thus “context remaining” drains to compaction after only about a quarter of the model’s actual window.

For everyday work, try:

```bash
claude --effort high
```

or `/effort medium` inside the session. Reserve `max` for genuinely difficult tasks. Also, Fable’s raw token count can look alarming while its cache reads are unusually cheap—but output/thinking remains expensive at $50/M tokens. [Fable 5.1 specifications](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-1/overview)
yeah i'm noticing very rapid context consumption at xhigh thinking. I'm compacting context early to avoid fade at fuller contexts and keep costs/usage down.

That makes sense—the 256k threshold is deliberate, not an accidental waste of Fable’s 1M window.

At `xhigh`, Fable generates substantial hidden reasoning, and its previous thinking blocks remain in the conversation and count toward later context. In a tool-heavy session, this compounds quickly:

`thinking → tool output → retained thinking → next turn rereads it all`

Early compaction breaks that snowball and may preserve answer quality before long-context degradation appears.

The tradeoff is that compaction generates a summary and resets much of the prompt cache. Because Fable 5.1’s cache reads are very cheap, early compaction isn’t guaranteed to minimize billed cost—but it can still reduce active-context growth and subscription usage. Anthropic’s [guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-1) acknowledges that this needs workload-specific testing.

Your **256k at `xhigh`** seems like a reasonable quality-first operating point. I’d combine it with dynamic effort:

- `high` for repository exploration and routine tool loops.
- `xhigh` for difficult diagnosis, design, and final synthesis.
- Compact at phase boundaries when possible, before a large retained reasoning trail becomes irrelevant.

That should be more efficient than holding `xhigh` throughout while preserving the anti-fade benefit you want.

content.text:
Not directly in either stock CLI. The active model can recognize a phase boundary, but neither Claude Code nor Codex exposes compaction as a model-callable tool.

| Harness | Native behavior |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | Fixed token-triggered auto-compaction, or user-run `/compact [focus]`. `PreCompact`/`PostCompact` hooks can observe, block, or react—but cannot initiate compaction. [Claude hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) |
| Codex | Fixed `model_auto_compact_token_limit`, or user-run `/compact`. There is no semantic trigger or compaction tool available to the model. [OpenAI configuration reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference), [Codex commands](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli) |

The practical hybrid is:

1. Instruct the model to announce clean phase boundaries and provide compaction focus text.
2. You invoke `/compact`.
3. Keep the 256k automatic threshold as a safety net.

For example, in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`:

```md
At a clean phase boundary, when substantial earlier detail is no longer
needed, recommend context compaction. Include one short `Preserve:` line
covering the active goal, completed work, decisions, verification results,
open problems, and exact next step. Do not recommend compaction merely
because a turn ended.
```

Claude could then say:

```text
Compaction recommended.
Preserve: implementation is complete; tests X/Y pass; Z remains; next run…
```

You would enter:

```text
/compact preserve implementation state, decisions, test results, open problems, and exact next step
```

For genuinely automatic phase-aware compaction, you’d need a custom controller: have the model emit a structured `phase_complete` signal, then let the controller invoke the provider’s compaction API. OpenAI explicitly recommends compacting after major milestones, but that orchestration is not currently exposed by the Codex CLI. Anthropic’s native server-side trigger is likewise token-based only. [OpenAI compaction guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model?model=gpt-5.2), [Anthropic compaction API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction)

A good policy would be `phase complete AND context > 100–150k`, with the existing 256k threshold as the hard fallback.

The two percentages are almost certainly using different denominators: your status line reports Fable’s full 1M context, while Claude’s auto-compaction indicator is using the configured 256k effective window minus reserved response space.
